newsitem.title: UK: Brent screen dip slows North Sea crude market.
newsitem.headline: Brent screen dip slows North Sea crude market.

text.p: A dip by Brent futures under $22 a barrel slowed European crude spot markets on Thursday, injecting caution into wet Brent business after three cargoes changed hands in the morning at steady levels, traders said.
March IPE Brent's dip below key resistance at 1455 GMT, the first time in four months it has fallen beneath $22 per barrel, helped depress forward Brent paper markets and narrow spreads.
March Brent was trading at $21.73 a barrel at 1842 GMT
"It's quiet because there is lots of focus on the outright price. And besides, there are not many cargoes left for sale. Everybody's waiting for the March programmes," a trader said.
Dated Brent was around five cents down at March +20/30 after the fall below $22.
Earlier in an active morning two cargoes loading Feb 17-19 and Feb 20-22 fetched March +28 and +32 cents respectively, with a third, loading Feb 19-21, changing hands at March +32.
Earlier Dated Brent had been steady with a European major offering a Feb 19-21 cargo at March +35. Dated Brent traded twice on Wednesday, at March +25 and +34 cents.
Intermonth spreads narrowed. Mar/Apr was discussed two cents easier at +36/+39, while Feb/Mar was talked five cents lower at +30/+40.
Paper March lost 14 cents to trade at $22.36 to the same Wall Street player seen buying heavily in recent days, after trading at $22.50 a barrel in late U.S. dealing on Wednesday.
Brent CFDs continued to weaken. Next week was talked three cents lower at March Brent +14/+16, with the week after discussed five cents lower at March -8/-4 cents.
One Brent cargo nominated loading dates of Feb 21-23 was clocked to Shell UK on Thursday.
Other North Sea crudes were quiet, with remaining February cargoes few and far between, traders said.
